description: Which components a generative-UI library may use to draw each router representation. The router picks the representation; the library's model then writes the UI only from the allowed components. A representation with no fitting component names a custom component to register instead of letting the model fake one.

libraries.name: OpenUI (OpenUI Lang)
libraries.installNote: Set OPENUI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 (or DO_NOT_TRACK=1) before installing: the packages' postinstall sends telemetry to PostHog.

data-table.note: Use EditableTable only when the use case allows editing.

decision-table.note: One row per rule in evaluation order, a column per condition and one for the outcome; say in the caption that the first matching row wins (DMN hit policy FIRST).

answer-receipt-card.note: One Card per run. CardHeader is the answer in one sentence, or a Callout saying the run failed and why. Under it two to four evidence lines, each a markdown link to its source. After a Separator, a one-line receipt: when it ran, on what (model, data version), how long, what it cost, and a link to the full trace.

link-directory.note: One card per group with a header; inside it, one line per item written as a markdown link [name](url) followed by one line on what is there. No detail pane, no table columns: the link is the whole detail.

argument-page.note: A Callout at the top states the page's one claim; then one Card per supporting section whose CardHeader is that section's sub-claim and whose body is the evidence (a number, quote, link or one Image). No dashboard grid.

master-detail.note: Table is the list; Tabs or Accordion hold the selected row's detail.

schema-explorer.note: One AccordionItem per entity, a Table of its fields inside.

requirements-traceability-matrix.note: Rows are requirements, columns are verifying items; mark cells with Tag.

upset-plot.note: OpenUI has no set-intersection chart: show intersection sizes as a sorted horizontal bar chart beside a membership table.

dot-plot.note: OpenUI has no dot marks for categories: horizontal bars stand in; sort them by value.

heatmap.note: OpenUI's library has no heatmap chart: use a Table of values, or register a custom heatmap.

interval-plot.note: OpenUI's charts draw no intervals: a Table with estimate, low and high columns sorted by estimate, and a Callout naming the interval (for example 95% confidence) and the reference value; or register a custom forest plot.

signed-effect-matrix.note: OpenUI has no diverging heatmap: a Table with the signed value in each cell (a plus or minus sign, not colour alone) and a Callout saying what each direction means; or register a custom diverging matrix.

small-multiples.note: One chart per panel inside a Stack, same axes and scale on every panel.

project-schedule.note: Steps for order, Table for dates and owners; no Gantt bars.

process-swimlane.note: Steps lose the lanes: name the owner in each step's text.

composite-linked-view.note: OpenUI views do not share selection; say so in the page.

libraries.checkedHow: Component names read from openuiLibrary.components in an installed @openuidev/react-ui 0.18.1, not from source folder names (the first map used folder names such as Charts, which OpenUI's parser rejects).

customComponentSources.GraphViewer: representation-router graph-viewer (typed-graph/v1): build it with defineGraphViewerComponent from graph-viewer/src/openui.mjs and register it with OpenUI's library.extend({ components: { add: [{ component, slots: ['Card.children'] }] } }). Edges read 'source label target' in the direction the question states.

libraries.restrictHow: Build the allowed library with openuiLibrary.extend({ components: { remove: <every known component not allowed> } }) and generate the model's prompt from that library, so the model never sees the others.
